name: compare-stats
description:
The metrics of text-stats, mine against the competitors: a row per metric.

tolerance: how far from the norm a metric is still within, a share of the norm (0.3 is ±30 %).
norm: «median» (the default) or «mean»: what delta and the verdict are against.
no_digits: leave out the words with a digit of every count, as text-stats does.
exclude: words to leave out of every count, as text-stats does.

The columns: metric; mine; median, mean, min, max, the metric over the competitors; delta, mine - the norm; verdict, «below», «within» or «above», mine against norm x (1 ± tolerance), and when the norm is 0, «within» if mine is 0, else «above». Numbers are rounded to 4 decimals; the counts (chars, chars_no_spaces, words, unique) stay whole numbers where they are whole.

Example: semkit read --whole mine.txt compare-stats competitors.csv write -
-> chars, 46, 44, 34.6667, 14, 46, 2, within; chars_no_spaces, 40, 38, 30.3333, 13, 40, 2, within; words, 6, 7, 5.3333, 2, 7, -1, within; unique, 5, 4, 3.6667, 2, 5, 1, within; water, 0.0, 0.1429, 0.0952, 0.0, 0.1429, -0.1429, below; nausea_classic, 1.41, 1.41, 1.38, 1.0, 1.73, 0.0, within; nausea_academic, 0.3333, 0.4286, 0.4048, 0.2857, 0.5, -0.0952, within; ttr, 0.8333, 0.8333, 0.8333, 0.6667, 1.0, 0.0, within; mtld, 10.08, 6.0, 5.36, 0.0, 10.08, 4.08, above; zipf, 70.9, 0.0, 23.6333, 0.0, 70.9, 70.9, above

competitors: a file with the texts of the competitors, one per row, in its column text, else in its first text column that is no url column; the file is read like `read` does. A url column, if the file has one, names the columns of --per-text.

The step takes the working column as my text (its cells, one per line); the table of the comparison replaces the current one.

options.name: --competitors
options.description: a file with the texts of the competitors, one per row, in its column text, else in its first text column that is no url column; the file is read like `read` does. A url column, if the file has one, names the columns of --per-text.

options.name: --tolerance
options.description: how far from the norm a metric is still within, a share of the norm (0.3 is ±30 %).

options.name: --norm
options.description: «median» (the default) or «mean»: what delta and the verdict are against.

options.name: --no-digits
options.description: leave out the words with a digit of every count, as text-stats does.

options.name: --exclude
options.description: words to leave out of every count, as text-stats does. Items: a comma list 'a,b', @FILE (one item per line, or the first column of a table) or @NAME of a list.

arguments.name: COMPETITORS
arguments.description: a file with the texts of the competitors, one per row, in its column text, else in its first text column that is no url column; the file is read like `read` does. A url column, if the file has one, names the columns of --per-text. The same as --competitors COMPETITORS.
